# Qi2 vs. Qi2.2 vs. MagSafe

**Qi2** is the Wireless Power Consortium's (WPC) wireless charging standard with a magnetic ring that snaps the phone into alignment. It charges at up to 15W. The magnet design came from Apple's MagSafe technology ([The Verge](https://www.theverge.com/news/708060/qi-2-2-certification-25w-wpc-belkin-anker-ugreen-aukey)).

**Qi2.2** is the newer version of Qi2, also branded **Qi2 25W**. It keeps the magnets but raises the speed limit to 25W, which the WPC says can take a phone from 0 to 50% in about 30 minutes. The first products were certified in July 2025 ([WPC](https://www.wirelesspowerconsortium.com/standards/qi-wireless-charging/)).

**MagSafe** is Apple's own brand and program, not a separate wireless standard. Apple certifies MagSafe accessories, and per [Macworld](https://www.macworld.com/article/668980/best-magsafe-chargers.html), certified chargers include an NFC antenna so the iPhone can identify them. They also have a magnetometer to prevent compass interference. Apple's current MagSafe Charger is certified for Qi2 25W, so in practice the two are now nearly the same thing on Apple's side ([Apple](https://www.apple.com/shop/product/mgdm4ll/a/magsafe-charger-2-m)).

## What speed you actually get (iPhone)
Per [Apple Support](https://support.apple.com/en-ie/105047):
- **25W:** iPhone 16 Plus, 16 Pro Max, 17, 17 Pro, 17 Pro Max, and 18 Pro models. This needs a 30W or greater adapter.
- **22.5W:** iPhone 16 and 16 Pro.
- **20W:** iPhone Air.
- **15W:** iPhone 17e and iPhone 15 and earlier, back to iPhone 12.

Also note that the iPhone 16e has no magnetic charging ([Macworld](https://www.macworld.com/article/668980/best-magsafe-chargers.html)).

## Watch for "MagSafe-compatible"
Chargers labeled only "MagSafe-compatible" are usually uncertified 7.5W models with a magnet ring. They work, and they're often cheaper, but they charge about half as fast as certified 15W chargers ([Macworld](https://www.macworld.com/article/668980/best-magsafe-chargers.html)). To check, look for the Qi2 logo or search the [WPC product database](https://www.wirelesspowerconsortium.com/standards/qi-wireless-charging/).

## Android
Support is limited. Per [The Verge](https://www.theverge.com/gadgets/939362/best-magsafe-qi2-2-batteries-power-banks):
- The Pixel 10, 10 Pro, and 10 Pro Fold support Qi2 at 15W.
- The Pixel 10 Pro XL supports Qi2.2 at 25W.
- Samsung's Galaxy S26 series is "Qi2 Ready," so it needs a magnetic case to get up to 15W.

## Which should you buy?
Get a Qi2.2/Qi2 25W-certified charger, which is backward compatible with 15W Qi2 and with older Qi phones. One option is the [Apple MagSafe Charger](https://www.apple.com/shop/product/mgdm4ll/a/magsafe-charger-2-m) (2 m listed at $49), which is certified for Qi2 25W. You'll need to buy a 30W USB-C adapter separately to get the full 25W.

If you tell me your phone model, I can say which speed you'd get and suggest a specific charger.
